questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Constitution guarantees six fundamental rights to its citizens.
 
• The rights mentioned are Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• There is no fundamental right called "Right to exploitation"; the correct term is "Right against Exploitation".
 
• The Right against Exploitation prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality:**

 
 
• It includes equality before law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom:**
 
 
• It includes freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association or union, movement, residence, and the right to practice any profession or occupation.
 
• Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation:**
 
 
• It prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.
 
• Articles 23 and 24 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion:**
 
 
• It ensures religious freedom and secularism in India.
 
• Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:**
 
 
• It allows individuals to go to the courts for enforcement of the fundamental rights against the state.
 
• Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution cover this right.

questions.question: Harshavardhana tried to cross the Narmada to march into the Deccan, but was stopped by a ruler belonging to the Chalukya dynasty, ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Pulakeshin II.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakeshin II, the King of the Chalukya dynasty defeated Harshavardhana when he seeks to enlarge his Empire into the southern peninsula of India.
 
• He defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada river in 618 AD.
 
• The Aihole inscription was written by Ravikirti, court poet of Chalukya King Pulakesin II who reigned from 610 to 642 CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**__

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He, at the young age of 25, captured Pataliputra from the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, Dhanananda.
 
• In this task, he was assisted by Kautilya, who was also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.
 
 
 
• Samudragupta 
 
 
• He was the first significant ruler of the Gupta Dynasty.
 
• Having come to the throne, he decided to extend the boundaries of his empire to cover the multiple kingdoms and republics that existed outside its pale.
 
• Known as the Napoleon of India for his conquests, he was also a man of many talents and laid a firm foundation for the empire.

questions.question: Ujjain was the capital of ancient Avanti and was ruled by

options.text: More than one of the above.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__King Vikramaditya.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)**

__
 
• **Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)**, was the son of Samudragupta and Datta Devi, who ruled from **380-412 A.D**.
 
• **Fa-Hien**, a Buddhist from China visited India during his reign. He recorded the prosperity of the Gupta Empire.
 
• His other names (as mentioned in coins) include** Vikrama, Devagupta, Devaraja, Simhavikrama, Vikramaditya Sakari**, etc.
 
• Chandragupta II was known for his deep interest in art and culture and nine gems or** Navratna** adorned his court.
 
• The nine Ratnas were: **Amarsimha, Dhanvantri, Harisena, Kalidas, Kahapanaka, Sanku, Varahamihira, Vararuchi, Vetalbhatta.**
 
• **Ujjain was the capital of the ancient Avanti kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.** It was located in the Malwa region of central India, on the banks of the Shipra River.
 
• Ujjain was a major cultural and intellectual center in ancient India. It was home to many scholars and poets, and it was also a center of trade and commerce.
 
• **The most famous ruler of Ujjain was King Vikramaditya, who ruled from 380 to 413 CE.** He was a great conqueror and a patron of the arts and sciences. Under his rule, Ujjain became one of the most prosperous and influential cities in India.
 
• King Vikramaditya is often depicted as a just and wise ruler. He is also said to have been a great scholar and a patron of the arts. The Vikram Samvat, a calendar still used in some parts of India, is named after him.
 
• Here are some additional details about King Vikramaditya:
 
 
• His real name was Chandragupta II.
 
• He was the son of Samudragupta, the greatest ruler of the Gupta Empire.
 
• He was a great conqueror and extended the Gupta Empire to its greatest extent.
 
• He was a patron of the arts and sciences and attracted many scholars and poets to his court.
 
• He was known for his wisdom and justice.
 
• He is often depicted as a just and wise ruler in Indian literature and folklore.

questions.question: Which of the following indicators is more effective when comparing the economic development between two countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Domestic Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross domestic product (GDP) **is a more helpful economic indicator than gross national product (GNP), which is primarily used to analyse a country's people's total income over a period of time.
 
• In addition to GDP,** the Consumer Price Index (CPI)**, which gauges pricing power and inflation, and the Monthly Unemployment Report, which includes weekly non-farm payrolls, are two additional important indicators of economic activity.
 
• The amount of money earned per person in a country or region is referred to as per capita income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Per capita income** can be used to calculate an area's average per-person income and to assess the population's level of living and quality of life. 
 
• **GDP** is a monetary measure of the monetary worth of final products and services (i.e., those purchased by the end user) produced in a country over a period of time.
 
• **The infant mortality rate (IMR)** is the number of deaths among children under the age of one per 1,000 live births. The rate for a specific region is calculated by dividing the number of children under the age of one by the number of live births during the year and multiplying by 1,000.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Ecological succession is defined as:

options.text: process by which geological changes take place
process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time
process by which the many species get extinct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "__**process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time**__". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecological succession**__ is defined as t__**he process by which the mix of species and habitat in an area changes over time**__.

 __
 
• The mechanism through which a** region's species** and habitat mix **evolve** throughout time is called** ecological succession**.
 
• These species eventually replace each other until a "**climax community**" is attained, such as a full forest, or until a **disruption**, such as a fire, happens.
 
• Or we can say that ecological succession is the process by which a biological community's **composition changes** as time passes.
 
• **Primary** and **secondary** succession has been identified as two distinct forms. In situations where the** soil** is **unable **to support life due to reasons like lava flows, recently formed sand dunes, or boulders left behind by a receding glacier, **primary succession** takes place.
 
• **Secondary succession** happens in places where an earlier **community** has been **eliminated**; it is characterized by relatively small disruptions that do not completely wipe out the environment's life and nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 __**Process**__
 __**Description**__
 
 

 **Process of ecological changes**
 Events known as **geological processes** take place over a period of time that can range from millions of years to thousands of kilometers.
 
 

 **Process of deforestation**
 When people **clear** or thin **forests** to make lumber or to use the land where the trees once stood for farming, grazing, extraction (of minerals, oil, or gas), or development as a result of population growth and migration, this is known as **deforestation**.
 
 

 **Process of extinction of species**
 A **species** goes extinct when it **disappears** from the planet. When a species' population declines as a result of environmental factors such as habitat fragmentation, climate change, natural disasters, etc. The** dinosaur** is among the most well-known instances of an **extinct species**.

questions.question: The position when the Earth is farthest from the Sun is known as:
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Aphelion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aphelion
 
 
• It is the point of Earth's orbit that is farthest from the Sun.
 
• When the earth reaches aphelion, the sun appears slightly smaller in the sky at any other time of year.
 
• The earth reaches aphelion only once a year.
 
• It happens near of 4th of July.
 
 
 
• Perihelion
 
 
• It is where the Earth is closest to the Sun (91.4 million miles, or 147 million kilometers). 
 
• This occurs around January 3 every year.
 
• The closest point to the Sun in a planet’s orbit is called perihelion. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5fb2bf1251ae70ac436ce9e42c1f77b56885b837439caf8afe84a8748637927.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Equinox
 
 
• It refers to a day with an equal duration of day and night.
 
• There are two equinoxes in a year:
 
• The entire **earth **experiences equal **day **and equal **night**.
 
• It occurs on the **21st of March** and **September 23rd**.
 
 
 
• Solstice
 
 
• ​It is the time of the year when the sun is farthest from the equatorial giving the long days or nights.
 
• It happens twice a year
 
• Summer Solstice ( June 21)
 
• Winter Solstice( December 22)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The earth is at the largest distance from the sun (Aphelion point) on the 4th of July.
 
• The Earth is closest to the Sun at its Perihelion about 2 weeks after the December Solstice.
 
• The Earth is farthest from the Sun – at its Aphelion – about 2 weeks after the June Solstice.

questions.question: Which of the following countries will now co-host the rescheduled 2026 Rugby League World Cup along with Australia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Papua New Guinea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2026 Rugby League World Cup was initially awarded to France, but due to financial challenges, it was reallocated to new hosts.
 
• Australia and Papua New Guinea will co-host the rescheduled tournament in 2026.
 
• Papua New Guinea is one of the few countries where rugby league is the national sport and enjoys a massive following.
 
• The inclusion of Papua New Guinea as a co-host highlights its strong rugby league culture and the region's importance to the sport.
 
• The event will feature both men's and women's tournaments, promoting inclusivity and global participation in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rugby League World Cup:**

 
 
• The Rugby League World Cup is an international tournament organized by the International Rugby League (IRL).
 
• The first Rugby League World Cup was held in 1954 in France, making it the oldest rugby world championship.
 
• The competition features national teams from around the world, with Australia traditionally being the dominant team.
 
 
 
• **Papua New Guinea's Rugby League Culture:**
 
 
• Rugby league is the national sport of Papua New Guinea, with deep cultural and social significance.
 
• The country has a professional rugby league team, the PNG Hunters, which competes in the Queensland Cup in Australia.
 
 
 
• **2026 Rugby League World Cup:**
 
 
• The tournament will feature men's, women's, and wheelchair competitions.
 
• It aims to expand the global appeal of rugby league while emphasizing diversity and inclusivity.
 
• Hosting matches in both Australia and Papua New Guinea will help grow the sport's presence in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
 
 
• **International Rugby League (IRL):**
 
 
• The IRL is the global governing body for rugby league, responsible for organizing international tournaments.
 
• The IRL works to develop the sport globally, focusing on emerging markets and grassroots initiatives.

questions.question: When was the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) scheme launched to promote affordable regional air travel in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**October 2016.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **More than one crore 49 lakh passengers have benefited from the UDAN scheme, launched to promote affordable regional air connectivity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The UDAN scheme was launched in October 2016 by the Government of India.**
 
• It aims to provide connectivity to unserved and underserved regions through revival of existing airstrips and airports.
 
• A total of 625 UDAN routes have been operationalised connecting 90 airports across the country.
 
• India’s airport network expanded from 74 airports in 2014 to 159 airports in 2024 under initiatives including UDAN.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• About UDAN Scheme__

 __
 
• UDAN stands for "Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik".
 
• Objective is to make air travel affordable and widespread, particularly in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
 
• Supports regional connectivity by offering financial incentives to airlines for operating flights on regional routes.
 
• Implemented by the Ministry of Civil Aviation with support from State Governments and airport operators.
 
 
 
• Key Achievements__
 
 
• More than 1.49 crore passengers have benefited till date.
 
• Expansion of India's airport network helping regional economic growth and job creation.
 
• Focus on reviving unserved and underserved airports to increase accessibility.

Choose the __incorrect pair__ from the following:

 
 

 
 Tribal Movements
 Year

 Kol Rebellion
 1831-32

 Bastar Rebellion
 1800

 1855

questions.solution:
The incorrect pair is __**option B.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bastar Rebellion:**__

 __
 
• ​​The **Bastar Rebellion,** also known as the Bastar Uprising, took place in **1910** in the Bastar region of present-day Chhattisgarh, India.
 
• It was an armed revolt led by the indigenous tribal population against the oppressive policies of the British colonial administration.
 
• The Bastar region, located in central India, was inhabited by various indigenous tribes, including the **Gond, Maria, and Muria tribes.**
 
• These tribes had a distinct **socio-cultural identity** and had traditionally governed themselves under their own systems.
 
• However, with the arrival of British colonial rule, their autonomy and way of life were significantly disrupted.
 
• The rebellion continued for several months, with sporadic clashes between the rebels and the British forces.
 
• However, due to the overwhelming military strength of the colonial forces and the lack of external support for the tribal fighters, the rebellion gradually lost momentum.
 
• 
 
**Gunda Dhur and Lachhu Uike **were eventually captured by the British forces in **1912** and sentenced to life imprisonment.

 
 
 

So the correct answer is **option B__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kol Rebellion:**__

 __
 
• ​The Kol Rebellion of **1831** was an uprising in the central provinces of British India, led by the Kol tribe.
 
• Fueled by grievances over oppressive land revenue policies and discriminatory practices, the rebellion aimed to challenge British rule and assert tribal rights.
 
• The Kols, armed with traditional weapons, launched attacks on colonial administration, disrupting revenue collection and targeting British officials.
 
• The rebellion was eventually suppressed through military force, leading to the arrest and execution of rebel leaders.
 
• Though short-lived, the Kol Rebellion highlighted the deep-seated discontent among **marginalized communities** and served as a precursor to future anti-colonial movements in India.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Rebellion:**__
 __
 
• ​The Santhal Rebellion of **1855 **was an armed uprising by the Santhal tribe in British India.
 
• It was sparked by land disputes, **oppressive policies, and forced labour.**
 
• The rebellion was violently suppressed by the colonial authorities, resulting in significant loss of life among the Santhal people.
 
 
 
• **Warli Rebellion:**__​
 
 
• ​The Warli Rebellion of **1940** was an indigenous uprising by the Warli tribe in British India.
 
• It was a protest against** oppressive land revenue policies **and forced labour.
 
• The rebellion was met with brutal repression by the colonial authorities, leading to casualties among the Warli community.

questions.question: Which of the following is a food-borne disease caused by the consumption of contaminated food or beverages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholera**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Cholera is a food-borne disease caused by consuming water or food contaminated **with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
 
• It** leads to severe diarrhoea and dehydration.**
 
• **The disease is commonly spread in areas with poor sanitation** and unsafe water supplies
 
• he hallmark symptoms of cholera include profuse watery diarrhoea, often described as "rice water stools," vomiting, and severe dehydration.
 
• If left untreated, dehydration can lead to shock, kidney failure, and death, sometimes within hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis** is an infectious disease caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*.

 
 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can spread to other parts of the body.
 
• The disease is transmitted through airborne particles when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
 
 
 
• **Chicken pox** is a highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus. It causes an itchy rash with red spots and blisters.
 
 
• The disease spreads through direct contact with an infected person or through the air by respiratory droplets.
 
 
 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic disease caused by *Plasmodium* species, transmitted through the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito.
 
 
• It affects red blood cells and causes symptoms like fever, chills, and anemia, predominantly in tropical and subtropical regions.
